title: Unexpected type binding when wrapping functions
body:

  instead.
  Please also consider:

  - checking our common issues page: https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html
  - searching our issue tracker: https://github.com/python/mypy/issues to see if
    it's already been reported
  - asking on gitter chat: https://gitter.im/python/typing
-->

**Bug Report**

I admit that I do not know if this is a bug, and not just my incomplete understanding of how the type system works, but I have run into some unexpected behaviour, and behaviour where mypy and pyre disagree, so it might be a bug.

I am writing code that lifts functions `T -> R` to `Optional[T] -> Optional[R]` in various ways, and when I write wrapper functions, type variables get bound in ways I didn't expect. It is particularly bad when I add protocols for various types on top of it, but I can create the unexpected behaviour without it. Basically, the issue is that if I write a function that changes a `Callable[[T], R]` into a `Callable[[Optional[T]], Optional[R]]`, and then apply such a function to another generic function `Callable[[T],R]` the type variables are no longer generic, and I cannot apply the wrapped function. This happens both when I work with wrapper functions or when I implement the wrapper as a `Generic` class.

**To Reproduce**

If I write a wrapper with a function, it might look like this:

```python
from typing import (
    TypeVar, 
    Protocol, Generic, 
    Optional as Opt
)


_T = TypeVar('_T')

class _F(Protocol[_T]):
    def __call__(self, __x: _T) -> _T:
        ...

# Lifting with a function...
def lift(f: _F[_T]) -> _F[Opt[_T]]:
    # This function would do more, but I just return f for the
    # type checking example
    return f # type: ignore
```

I get the desired behaviour if I wrap a function with a concrete type


```python
def f(x: int) -> int:
    return x

reveal_type(lift(f))  # _F[Opt[int]] -- as expected
```

but if I use a generic type, the wrapped function is not generic:

```python
def g(x: _T) -> _T:
    return x

reveal_type(lift(g)) # _F[Union[_T`-1,None]] -- _T is bound (incorrectly?)
                     # pyre thinks this is _F[None] which is also odd...
lift(g)(1)  # so won't accept int
```

**Expected Behavior**

I was expecting the wrapped function to have the type `Callable[[Opt[_T]], Opt[_T]]` and in particular I would expect to be able to call it with an `int` argument.

**To Reproduce**

If I use a `Generic` class for the lifted function, it can look like this:

```python
# Moving generic type to Generic...
class lifted(Generic[_T]):
    """Lift type _T to Opt[_T]."""

    def __init__(self, f: _F[_T]) -> None:
        self._f = f

    def __call__(self, x: Opt[_T], /) -> Opt[_T]:
        """Call lifted."""
        return self._f(x) # type: ignore

reveal_type(lifted[_T])  # _F[T?] -> lifted[_T?]
```

and it will work for a function with a concrete type, like `f: int -> int` above

```python
reveal_type(lifted(f))          # lifted[int] -- perfect
reveal_type(lifted(f).__call__) # Opt[int] -> Opt[int] -- perfect
lifted(f)(1)                    # We can call with int
lifted(f)(None)                 # We can call with None
```

but things get crazy when I use a generic function like `g: _T -> _T`:

```python
reveal_type(lifted(g))            # lifted[_T`1] -- _T is bound!
                                  # pyre thinks (correctly I think) it is lifted[_T]
reveal_type(lifted(g).__call__)   # Opt[_T`1] -> Opt[_T`1]
                                  # pyre says Any -> Any which I suppose is fine
lifted(g)(1)                      # incompatible type, int isn't an Opt[_T]
                                  # pyre seems to accep this one
lifted(g)(None)                   # but at least None is in Opt[_T]...

reveal_type(lifted[_T](g))          # lifted[_T?] -- Ok
reveal_type(lifted[_T](g).__call__) # def (None) ???
                                    # pyre: Opt[_T] -> Opt[_T] as expected

lifted[_T](g)(1)             # incompatible type "int"; expected "None"
lifted[_T](g)(None)          # but at least None works...
# Pyre doesn't like the [_T] here but accepts the calls without it...
```

**Expected Behavior**

Again, I would expect the `Generic` `lifted` class to accept types that match the wrapped function's type. This is more important when I need to add protocols to the types, but I would also expect it to work here.

**Your Environment**

I tested this in [mypy playground](https://mypy-play.net/?mypy=latest&python=3.10&gist=48dc95420afde2911df5b9a72f42e78c) and [pyre playground](https://pyre-check.org/play?input=from%20typing%20import%20(%0A%20%20%20%20TypeVar%2C%20%0A%20%20%20%20Protocol%2C%20Generic%2C%20%0A%20%20%20%20Optional%20as%20Opt%0A)%0A%0A%0A_T%20%3D%20TypeVar(%27_T%27)%0A%0Aclass%20_F(Protocol%5B_T%5D)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20__call__(self%2C%20__x%3A%20_T)%20-%3E%20_T%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20...%0A%0A%23%20Lifting%20with%20a%20function...%0Adef%20lift(f%3A%20_F%5B_T%5D)%20-%3E%20_F%5BOpt%5B_T%5D%5D%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20This%20function%20would%20do%20more%2C%20but%20I%20just%20return%20f%20for%20the%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20type%20checking%20example%0A%20%20%20%20return%20f%20%23%20type%3A%20ignore%0A%0Adef%20f(x%3A%20int)%20-%3E%20int%3A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20x%0Adef%20g(x%3A%20_T)%20-%3E%20_T%3A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20x%0A%0Areveal_type(lift(f))%20%23%20_F%5BOpt%5Bint%5D%5D%20--%20as%20expected%0Areveal_type(lift(g))%20%23%20_F%5BUnion%5B_T%60-1%2CNone%5D%5D%20--%20_T%20is%20bound%20(incorrectly)%0Alift(g)(1)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20so%20won%27t%20accept%20int%0A%0A%0A%23%20Moving%20generic%20type%20to%20Generic...%0Aclass%20lifted(Generic%5B_T%5D)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Lift%20type%20_T%20to%20Opt%5B_T%5D.%22%22%22%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20__init__(self%2C%20f%3A%20_F%5B_T%5D)%20-%3E%20None%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20self._f%20%3D%20f%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20__call__(self%2C%20x%3A%20Opt%5B_T%5D%2C%20%2F)%20-%3E%20Opt%5B_T%5D%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Call%20lifted.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20self._f(x)%20%23%20type%3A%20ignore%0A%0Areveal_type(lifted%5B_T%5D)%20%20%23%20_F%5BT%3F%5D%20-%3E%20lifted%5B_T%3F%5D%0A%0Adef%20h(x%3A%20_T)%20-%3E%20_T%3A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20x%0A%0Areveal_type(lifted(f))%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20lifted%5Bint%5D%20--%20perfect%0Areveal_type(lifted(f).__call__)%20%23%20Opt%5Bint%5D%20-%3E%20Opt%5Bint%5D%20--%20perfect%0Alifted(f)(1)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20We%20can%20call%20with%20int%0Alifted(f)(None)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20We%20can%20call%20with%20None%0A%0Areveal_type(lifted(g))%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20lifted%5B_T%601%5D%20--%20_T%20is%20bound!%0Areveal_type(lifted(g).__call__)%20%20%20%23%20Opt%5B_T%601%5D%20-%3E%20Opt%5B_T%601%5D%0Alifted(g)(1)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20incompatible%20type%2C%20int%20isn%27t%20an%20Opt%5B_T%5D%0Alifted(g)(None)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20but%20at%20least%20None%20is%20in%20Opt%5B_T%5D...%0A%0Areveal_type(lifted%5B_T%5D(g))%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20lifted%5B_T%3F%5D%20--%20Ok%0Areveal_type(lifted%5B_T%5D(g).__call__)%20%23%20def%20(None)%20%3F%3F%3F%0A%0Alifted(g)(1)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20incompatible%20type%20%22int%22%3B%20expected%20%22None%22%0Alifted(g)(None)%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20but%20at%20least%20None%20works...%0A)
